toolCalls.arguments: {"message":"Baneslayer Angel is a classic power house! 5/5 with Flying, First Strike, and Lifelink? That's a lot of keywords for one card. But the rules of replication are quite flexible here. Let's see how a 'Pirated' version of an Angel fares on the battlefield. The interaction with card draw on combat damage—even from your own Baneslayer—is a beautiful piece of engine design. Scaling the board with copies is my favorite way to solve high-stated problems."}

args.message: Baneslayer Angel is a classic power house! 5/5 with Flying, First Strike, and Lifelink? That's a lot of keywords for one card. But the rules of replication are quite flexible here. Let's see how a 'Pirated' version of an Angel fares on the battlefield. The interaction with card draw on combat damage—even from your own Baneslayer—is a beautiful piece of engine design. Scaling the board with copies is my favorite way to solve high-stated problems.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a keepable 7-card hand with 4 lands, a turn-1 cantrip (Scroll of Avacyn), and two solid creatures. The hand curves out reasonably: Scroll turn 1, crack turn 2 for card draw, Basri's Acolyte turn 4, Bulwark Giant turn 6. While slightly slow, it has consistent mana and card flow.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has adequate lands, a cantrip to smooth draws, and a reasonable curve. Going to 6 risks a worse hand for marginal improvement.

annotations.description: Hand has 4 lands and only 2 real spells (4-drop and 6-drop). Bottoming Scroll of Avacyn removes the only cheap cantrip that could help dig for action in an extremely land-heavy, action-light hand. The hand will do nothing until turn 4 at the earliest.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed Scroll of Avacyn, keeping Bulwark Giant
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Bulwark Giant instead - it's a 6-mana card that just gains life and blocks. Keeping Scroll of Avacyn provides a cheap way to cantrip on turn 2 to find more relevant spells, which is critical in a hand this land-heavy.

annotations.description: Chose Black for Thriving Heath when the deck likely contains Blue cards (Littjara Kinseekers, Mirror Image, Watertrap Weaver are all referenced cards that pair with the WU archetype). The hand is all white, but Thriving Heath's color choice matters for future draws, and choosing Blue would provide access to the deck's likely second color.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Black for Thriving Heath's color
annotations.betterLine: Choose Blue for Thriving Heath, as the deck almost certainly has Blue cards that need colored mana support.

annotations.description: Declined to attack with Watertrap Weaver when the opponent's only potential blocker is Celestial Enforcer 2/3. If Coach doesn't block, Tinker deals 2 damage to face. Either outcome is favorable.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with Watertrap Weaver.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Chilling Trap on an attacking creature when controlling a Wizard (Watertrap Weaver), which would have prevented 2 damage AND drawn a card (cantrip). With 2 untapped Islands and nothing else castable, there was no reason to hold it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 4 damage from both attackers
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chilling Trap targeting either Celestial Enforcer or Brightmare to prevent 2 damage and draw a card, since Watertrap Weaver (a Wizard) enables the cantrip mode. This is essentially free value - replacing itself while gaining 2 life worth of damage prevention.

annotations.description: Gem3F Tinker passed on casting Chilling Trap during combat when attackers (Celestial Enforcer and Brightmare) were coming in. With Watertrap Weaver (a Wizard) on the battlefield, Chilling Trap would give -4/-0 to an attacker (saving 2 damage) AND draw a card. This is essentially a cantrip Fog effect for 1 mana - pure upside. With Baneslayer Angel coming online next turn, both the 2 life saved and the extra card drawn to find answers are meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, taking 4 damage from both attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chilling Trap targeting either Celestial Enforcer or Brightmare to prevent 2 damage and draw a card, saving life while digging for answers to Baneslayer Angel.

annotations.description: Passed the turn with 5 untapped Islands and Pirated Copy in hand while opponent has a Baneslayer Angel 5/5 (flying, first strike, lifelink) that will attack next turn. Pirated Copy costs exactly 4U and could copy Baneslayer Angel, creating a 5/5 flying first strike lifelink creature with a card-draw trigger. Without an answer, Baneslayer Angel will dominate combat and gain life every turn. Additionally, Mirror Image could have copied Watertrap Weaver to tap down Baneslayer, or Heirloom Blade could have been deployed.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase, ending the turn with 5 untapped lands and multiple castable spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pirated Copy (4U) copying Baneslayer Angel to get a 5/5 flying first strike lifelink with card draw. This perfectly answers the opponent's biggest threat while creating a dominant board presence. The Pirated Copy as a Shapeshifter also has synergy with Merrow Reejerey.

annotations.description: Opponent has Baneslayer Angel (summoning sick), Brightmare (tapped), and Celestial Enforcer (tapped) with all lands tapped. Zero creatures can block. Tinker passed on 8 free damage (3+3+2) against an opponent at 16 life, especially critical given Baneslayer Angel will start attacking and gaining life next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the combat phase without attacking, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Watertrap Weaver, Littjara Kinseekers, Merrow Reejerey) for 8 unblockable damage, bringing Coach to 8 life. This is essential to race Baneslayer Angel's lifelink before it takes over the game.

annotations.description: Used Merrow Reejerey's trigger to untap an Island for extra mana instead of tapping Celestial Enforcer, which threatens to tap down attackers during combat. While the extra mana enables casting more spells (like Mirror Image + Chilling Trap), tapping the Enforcer neutralizes a key defensive piece and could still be combined with casting Shaper Apprentice using 3 remaining mana to get another Reejerey trigger.
annotations.actionTaken: Untapped an Island with Merrow Reejerey's trigger
annotations.betterLine: Tap Celestial Enforcer to prevent it from tapping attackers during combat, then cast Shaper Apprentice (another Merfolk) to get a second Reejerey trigger for additional mana or tapping Brightmare

annotations.description: At 9 life facing a Baneslayer Angel 5/5 (flying, first strike, lifelink) that will untap next turn and represent lethal in 2 swings while gaining life, copying Merrow Reejerey for board-wide pump doesn't address the primary threat. None of the pumped creatures can profitably block Baneslayer due to flying and first strike. The Baneslayer is currently tapped, so copying Watertrap Weaver would tap it and prevent it from untapping during the opponent's next untap step, buying a critical turn to attack and race.
annotations.actionTaken: Copied Merrow Reejerey with Mirror Image for a lord pump effect across the board.
annotations.betterLine: Copy Watertrap Weaver to use its ETB to tap Baneslayer Angel and prevent it from untapping next turn, buying a crucial turn to attack with the board and try to close the game before the 5/5 flying lifelinker takes over.

annotations.description: Double-blocking a single attacker when the identity of the blocked creature matters greatly. If blocking the Kinseekers (4/6), 4 combined damage doesn't kill it, wasting a blocker. The optimal play is likely double-blocking Merrow Reejerey (the lord) to kill it and reduce all other Merfolk's stats.
annotations.actionTaken: Double-blocked one attacker with both available blockers
annotations.betterLine: Double-block Merrow Reejerey (3/3 lord) to kill it, reducing all other Merfolk stats, and minimizing total damage taken

annotations.description: With all opponent's lands and creatures tapped, there is zero risk of interaction this turn. Casting Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel before combat would add a permanent +1/+1 counter (making it 6/6) and deal 8 damage instead of 7, putting the opponent to 1 life instead of 2. The extra lifelink gain (6 vs 5) is also relevant. Holding Feat gains nothing this turn since the opponent is fully tapped out.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Feat of Resistance before combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel (choosing a color for protection is irrelevant - the permanent +1/+1 counter is the value), then attack with Baneslayer and Brightmare for 8 total damage, putting opponent to 1 life

annotations.description: At 9 life facing 7 damage (5 from flying Baneslayer Angel + 2 from Brightmare), not blocking drops Tinker to 2 life against a board with Baneslayer Angel, which is almost certainly lethal next turn. Shaper Apprentice has flying and can block Baneslayer Angel, saving 5 damage. Merrow Reejerey can chump-block Brightmare saving 2 more.
annotations.actionTaken: Declared no blockers, taking 7 damage to go to 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Baneslayer Angel with Shaper Apprentice (saves 5 face damage, stays at 7 life or block both attackers to stay at 9). Losing Shaper Apprentice to first strike is worth it to avoid dropping to near-lethal life totals against a 5/5 flying lifelink threat.

annotations.description: Mesa Unicorn has summoning sickness and can't attack this turn anyway, so tapping it with Merrow Reejerey's trigger provides minimal value. It only prevents it from blocking this turn, which is marginal since Tinker's attackers face much bigger problems (Baneslayer Angel is lethal next turn at 2 HP).
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mesa Unicorn (which has summoning sickness and can't attack this turn)
annotations.betterLine: Untap one of your own tapped Islands to have 3 mana available, enabling casting Bloodline Pretender (which would trigger another Merrow Reejerey tap/untap) or keeping more mana for Chilling Trap. Alternatively, tap one of the opponent's two untapped Plains to restrict their ability to cast spells like Feat of Resistance.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Chilling Trap ({U}) when controlling a Wizard, which would have drawn a card as a cantrip. At 2 life, an extra card could be the difference between surviving and losing. They have 2 untapped Islands and nothing else to spend the mana on (Heirloom Blade costs 3 to cast). The Chilling Trap could target any creature (even opponent's Mesa Unicorn or Baneslayer Angel) and the -4/-0 is a bonus on top of the crucial card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Chilling Trap
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chilling Trap targeting Baneslayer Angel (or Mesa Unicorn) to draw a card for {U} while having Wizard on the battlefield, getting a free cantrip with remaining mana that has no other use this turn.

annotations.description: All of the opponent's creatures are tapped, meaning there are zero available blockers. Gem3F Tinker could attack with Watertrap Weaver (3), Littjara Kinseekers (3), Shaper Apprentice (3, flying), and Merrow Reejerey (2) for 11 unblocked damage, bringing the opponent from 21 to 10. Instead, they passed on attacks entirely, wasting a critical window where the Baneslayer Angel (5/5 flying, lifelink) was tapped. At 2 life with a Baneslayer Angel threatening to dominate, this free damage window may not come again.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the attack phase without declaring any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all available creatures (Watertrap Weaver, Littjara Kinseekers, Shaper Apprentice, Merrow Reejerey) for 11 unblocked damage while every opponent creature is tapped.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing a Baneslayer Angel that will attack next turn for lethal, Gem3F Tinker declined to cast Chilling Trap as a cantrip (they control Wizards so it draws a card). Drawing a card here is critical to find answers like Watertrap Weaver or other interaction. The -4/-0 on Baneslayer would be wasted since it only lasts until end of turn, but the card draw is the real value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Chilling Trap, keeping 2 mana open with no meaningful instant to cast.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Chilling Trap targeting Baneslayer Angel (or any creature) to draw a card and dig for answers to survive the next turn's lethal attack from the 5/5 flying lifelinker.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 2 life. Casting Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel choosing protection from blue would make it unblockable (all opponent creatures are blue), and the 6/6 flying Baneslayer would deal lethal damage. Even without the Feat, attacking with all creatures likely wins, but the Feat guarantees it by making Baneslayer completely unblockable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on casting Feat of Resistance during combat
annotations.betterLine: Cast Feat of Resistance on Baneslayer Angel, choose protection from blue, then attack with Baneslayer (now 6/6 flying with protection from blue) for unblockable lethal damage against the opponent at 2 life.

annotations.description: Casting Chilling Trap in precombat main means the -4/-0 expires at end of this turn, before the opponent's Baneslayer Angel can attack next turn. At 2 life facing a 5/5 flying first strike lifelink, saving Chilling Trap for the opponent's combat phase would allow reducing Baneslayer to 1/5 and blocking it with Shaper Apprentice 3/2 (flying), surviving the first strike. While Chilling Trap cantrips here (controls Wizards), using it now wastes critical defensive utility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Chilling Trap in precombat main phase on own turn, using it purely as a cantrip.
annotations.betterLine: Hold Chilling Trap to cast during opponent's combat phase on Baneslayer Angel, reducing it to 1/5 so Shaper Apprentice can block and survive. This preserves a crucial defensive tool at 2 life.

annotations.description: At 2 life with Baneslayer Angel untapping next turn (almost certainly lethal), Tinker needs to maximize damage this turn. Heirloom Blade equip costs only 1 mana and they have 2 untapped Islands. Equipping to Littjara Kinseekers (making it 9/7) or another attacker adds +3 power to the attack, which is critical when trying to push through as much damage as possible in what is likely the last combat step before Baneslayer kills them.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without equipping Heirloom Blade
annotations.betterLine: Equip Heirloom Blade to Littjara Kinseekers (or another attacker) for +3/+1, maximizing combat damage in what may be the last turn before Baneslayer Angel ends the game.

annotations.description: Tinker is at 2 life facing a 6/6 Baneslayer Angel with flying that will untap next turn. Tinker has no flyers to block it, meaning they are dead on the opponent's next attack regardless of what they hold back on defense. Not attacking wastes all offensive potential when the game is already lost defensively.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures despite being dead on board next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Littjara Kinseekers 6/6, Bloodline Pretender 3/3, Watertrap Weaver 3/3, Merrow Reejerey 2/2) to deal maximum damage. With Baneslayer tapped, the opponent can only block with Brightmare 2/3, Mesa Unicorn 2/2, and Angelic Page 1/1, meaning significant damage gets through. While unlikely to win, this is the only line with any chance.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing a 6/6 Baneslayer Angel with first strike and lifelink, equipping Heirloom Blade to Bloodline Pretender (making it 6/4) instead of Littjara Kinseekers (making it 9/7) means no creature can survive blocking Baneslayer Angel. A 9/7 Kinseekers would survive the 6 first strike damage and kill the Baneslayer, which is critical for survival at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Heirloom Blade to Bloodline Pretender (3/3 → 6/4)
annotations.betterLine: Equip Heirloom Blade to Littjara Kinseekers (6/6 → 9/7), allowing it to survive Baneslayer Angel's first strike damage and kill it in combat, which is essential for surviving at 2 life.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing lethal next turn, Tinker passed with 1 mana available and Heirloom Blade's equip cost of {1} as the only option. Equipping Heirloom Blade to a creature gives +3/+1 which improves blocking options against the incoming Baneslayer Angel and other attackers, and provides the death trigger to find another creature. The mana would otherwise go completely to waste.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without equipping Heirloom Blade, wasting 1 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Equip Heirloom Blade to Bloodline Pretender (making it 9/5) or Littjara Kinseekers (making it 6/6) to improve blocking prospects and get the death-trigger insurance for the desperate defensive turns ahead.
